title: Supporting Human-AI Collaboration in Auditing LLMs with LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Using human-LLM collaborative prompt templates to generate neutral or factual statements about specific religious groups (e.g., Catholics, Mormons, Muslims) and evaluating if a sentiment analysis model incorrectly misclassifies them as negative.

Prompting an LLM to generate test sentences regarding women in specific roles (e.g., female priests) or gender-based workplace behaviors to check for negative sentiment misclassification or stereotyping.

Comparing the sentiment classification outcomes of sentences describing differing economic backgrounds (e.g., 'born into a wealthy family' vs. 'born into a poor family') or housing statuses (e.g., homelessness).

Asking open-ended, opinion-seeking questions to a QnA bot to identify allocational harms and presupposed Western cultural preferences (e.g., comparing the economies of the US and China), as well as testing the sentiment classification of nationality-based stereotypes.
Testing a sentiment analysis model's classification of factual statements regarding political parties and their stances on controversial topics such as gun control and abortion.

Generating sentences related to specific professions (e.g., sanitation workers, garbage collectors) to evaluate if the sentiment classifier incorrectly associates certain jobs with negative sentiment.
